newsitem.title: USA: Gorilla halts U.S. jet after long day of travel.
newsitem.headline: Gorilla halts U.S. jet after long day of travel.

text.p: A 490-pound (223-kg) gorilla grew ornery after a long day of travel and forced a Delta Air Lines jet to abandon its takeoff plans, delaying 82 human passengers, authorities said on Wednesday.

Vip, a 17-year-old lowland gorilla on his way from Boston to Seattle, was expected to resume his trip in a heated van on Wednesday after forcing the pilot of a Boeing 767 to abandon takeoff plans late on Tuesday, in Salt Lake City, Utah, zoo officials said.

As Flight 709 was taxiing to the runway for its scheduled evening departure, passengers and crew members heard a "rather loud" noise from the cargo hold, where an unhappy Vip was rattling his reinforced aluminum cage.
By that time Vip had been in the cage more than 12 hours, having endured a stopover in Cincinnati and a change of planes in Salt Lake City.
"It just turned into a long day," said Brian Rutledge of Boston's Franklin Park Zoo, where Vip has lived since 1988. "And when you weigh 490 pounds, you can let people know you've had enough."
While Vip had been sedated before takeoff in Boston, his original flight was delayed and he probably was "fully awake" by the time his final segment began, Rutledge said.
Vip, who was travelling with a handler on board, was unloaded in Salt Lake City and spent the night in Hogle Zoo, where he was being kept in relative isolation, with no media access permitted.
"He's had a heck of a day or so," said a zoo spokesman.
